title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - control mapping + risk questions
content:
Notes to self - SOC2 prep (working draft)

Purpose:
- Collect open risk questions and a first-pass control mapping for our hosted API + dedicated/private offerings.
- Capture action items that need owners before next audit dry-run.

Top-level risks (brain dump):
1) Unauthorized access to customer data (API keys, embeddings, logs)
   - Potential controls: IAM least-privilege, key rotation, encryption at rest, audit logging for key usage.
2) Model / inference code changes causing data leakage or regressions
   - Potential controls: PR reviews, CI gating, canary rollouts, model validation tests, change management ticketing.
3) Inadequate segregation between hosted and private customer data
   - Potential controls: network partitioning, dedicated capacity options, data access reviews.
4) Incident detection & response gaps (slow detection for data exfiltration)
   - Potential controls: alerting, SIEM integration, runbooks, quarterly tabletop exercises.
5) Backup and restore for control plane metadata and customer configs
   - Potential controls: encrypted backups, periodic restore tests, documented RTO/RPO.

Control mapping (first pass) - correlate SOC2 common criteria to internal artifacts:
- Logical access (CC6/AC):
  * Owners: Priya/Infra. Artifacts: IAM policy docs, role definitions (confluence), onboarding/offboarding checklist (HR ticket).
  * Evidence to collect: role assignment logs, recent offboard tickets, privileged access reviews (last 90 days).
- Change management (CC8/CM):
  * Owners: Eng release engineering. Artifacts: github PRs, release tags, deploy runbooks, approvals in GitHub/Linear.
  * Evidence: merged PRs with approvals, release notes, rollback logs, CI test results for last 6 months.
- Encryption & key mgmt (CC7/SC-crypt):
  * Owners: Infra + Security. Artifacts: KMS config (cloud provider), key rotation policy, HSM integration notes for Private.
  * Evidence: rotation logs, encryption-at-rest confirmations, KMS access audit.
- Monitoring & logging (CC5/DM/Detection):
  * Owners: Observability team. Artifacts: dashboards, alert rules, retention policies.
  * Evidence: alert history, incident tickets, SIEM ingest examples.
- Vendor management (CC10/Vendors):
  * Owners: Legal + Procurement. Artifacts: vendor contracts, SOC2 reports from providers (cloud, logging).
  * Evidence: signed contracts, vendor due diligence notes.

Open questions / unknowns (need answers before mapping is final):
- What is the retention policy for raw inference request logs for hosted API (prod)? current config shows 90 days but need written policy to reference. (owner: Observability)
- For Dedicated customers using shared infra, do we have documented proof of network separation? (owner: Infra + SolutionsEng)
- Private deployment: how do we show customer-managed KMS integration evidence? do we need customer attestations or do we log config validation? (owner: Security + SolutionsEng)
- Backup evidence: when was the last successful restore test for control plane metadata? I have a note from 2025-07 but need 2026 test evidence. (owner: Release Eng/Infra)

Action items / todo (short-term):
- [ ] Assemble role review packet for access control (list of active admin roles + last usage) — due 2026-03-08 (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Confirm logs retention settings and produce a simple policy doc (owner: Observability - Lena) — due 2026-03-05
- [ ] Draft change management evidence checklist (what commits/PRs to sample) and share with release engineering — due 2026-03-10 (owner: Ryan)
- [ ] Identify vendor SOC2 reports (cloud provider, monitoring) and attach to confluence page — due 2026-03-04 (owner: Legal)
- [ ] Run a mini restore test for control plane configs and capture screenshots/logs — target week of 2026-03-15 (owner: Infra)

Sampling plan for evidence collection:
- Collect 3 months of samples for access logs and PR/merge evidence. Focus on high-risk services: hosted API, auth service, billing.
- For change mgmt, sample one major release and two minor patch cycles in last 6 months.

Draft notes for audit Qs (answers/short bullets):
Q: How do you restrict access to production keys?
A: Keys provisioned via cloud KMS with IAM roles; access to create/rotate keys restricted to infra/service accounts; human admin access requires approval via IAM group and ticket. Showing: KMS IAM policy, group membership export, recent rotation event.

Q: How do you ensure model changes don't degrade customer-facing outputs?
A: Pipeline includes unit + integration tests, staging canary rollouts, model perf/eval checks (automated evals against baseline prompts), rollback on regression. Evidence: perf dashboard, canary rollout logs, eval report.

Quick references / links (placeholders):
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC/SOC2-ONBOARD
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-56 (audit prep board)
- Slack: #security-soc2 channel (search thread: "external-audit-prep")
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789 (backup test script)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc messy — we'll iterate. Prefer working in Drive until mapping is stable, then move finalized evidence list to Confluence.
- Flag anything that requires exec sign-off (contracts, SLAs) and loop in Legal early.

Recent changes (log):
- 2026-02-20: added backup test TODO and vendor list.
- 2026-02-26: updated control mapping for change mgmt after conversation with release engineering.
- 2026-03-01: invited Priya & Lena as collaborators.

End of scratchpad.
